notes.summary: Canonical all-support envelope criterion and exact qualified smooth source reconstructed; no inherited-audit completion claimed.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves canonical primary/unit positivity before limits, equality of C/D raw suprema, every-degree convergence and the continuity/uniform/greatest-minorant equivalence. Reconstructs source CE and signed-model O(1/m) from the complete BFJ proof at smooth affine closed algebraically closed characteristic-zero germs, with closed-simplex continuity, all retractions and t=m+C. Completion, gauges and curve min(f,0) retain ENTIRE G331; these are foundations, not claimed novelty.
notes.text:
Use ENTIRE qualified G331, including every model, support, source, audit and radial qualification. C is its independently geometric continuous uniform cone and D its actual decreasing-C-net completion. Actual negative effective REAL Cartier presentations on directed ACTUAL primary blowups satisfy degree >=0 on EVERY contracted integral curve before comparison or limits. G331 supplies comparison, full-fibre positive descent, quotient-support lifting, completion and the primary cocycle; it supplies no envelope theorem. The following foundations are reconstructed, not claimed as new results.

On a nonempty full primary section X, for finite continuous signed f set B=max(0,-min f), A_m={b:v(b)+mf(v)>=0 for EVERY v}, A_0=R and h_m=-v(A_m)/m. These are ideals containing a^ceil(mB), with A_m A_n contained in A_(m+n). They are primary when f is negative somewhere and unit otherwise. Ideal-integrality follows by the uniquely least-valued leading term in a monic equation if v(b)<-mf(v); infinite values already satisfy the tests. On Bl_(A_m), -E_m/m is actual negative effective relatively ample, hence positive on EVERY contracted curve. Units give zero.

Rational primary/unit profiles are uniformly dense in C by G331. Approximate a C minorant and subtract a small negative rational boundary constant; common denominators give a rational ideal competitor. If -v(I)/r<=f, then I is contained in A_r. Consequently p(f)=sup_m h_m is the C raw supremum. For a D minorant inf_i g_i, the directed open sets {g_i<f+epsilon} cover compact X; one index works everywhere, and g_i-epsilon is a C minorant. Thus the D raw supremum is the same p. It is finite LSC, with -B<=p<=min(f,0). If M1=||v(A_1)|| and m=kr+s, 0<=s<r, grading gives h_m>=h_r-rM1/m. Hence every degree converges pointwise to p. With H_N=max_(r<=N)h_r, H_N-NM1/m<=h_m<=p. Compact strict-test covers show continuous p implies uniform convergence; the converse gives p in C. A greatest D minorant equals p and is USC, so LSC makes it continuous. Thus greatest C/D existence, continuous p and uniform canonical convergence are equivalent. Negative constant shifts give the 1-Lipschitz obstacle bound.

The smooth source is ONLY a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field. For signed primary models F, BFJ 1.14 fixes a simple complex and 1.15 gives uniform density. The max-directed weak-nef coefficients below Z(F), bounded below by a negative constant barrier, have a finite greatest weak-nef limit W. BFJ 3.11 gives substantive continuity on EACH CLOSED simplex. Using ALL retractions, H=inf_pi H_W(r_pi v) satisfies -B<=H<=F: extend divisorial bounds on every refined closed simplex and use F fixed by the original retraction. G331's full BFJ D comparison bounds every competitor by H.

Canonical completed ideals J_m equal L-infinity(mW)=L-infinity(mZ(F)) by BFJ 3.17. Divisorial tests imply all-support tests by truncating (b)+mhat^N with N>=mB, then applying continuity and G331's full divisorial density; primary contraction is exact. For nonzero W, 3.14 gives strict negativity and fixed-complex thinness gives A_thin<=-CW. The WHOLE 3.18 proof applies with real t=m+C: its (ii) uses this fixed-complex inequality and its (iii) applies (i) to tW. Therefore (1+C/m)W<=W_m<=W. Closed-simplex continuity and ALL-retraction infima give 0<=H-h_m<=CB/m on EVERY support. H is consequently continuous and geometric. Zero uses unit ideals; bottom is separate. Uniform signed-model approximation and Lipschitz prove source CE for all continuous obstacles. DVR/empty cases are direct; completion and primary gauges transport through G331. Historical resolution, multiplier subadditivity and smooth Izumi remain disclosed published dependencies, not recursively fresh proofs.

For primary b, d(v)=v(b)>0 and T(v)=v/d(v). Transport f_b(Tv)=f_a(v)/d(v); every canonical inequality divides by d, leaving ideals unchanged and dividing profiles/envelopes by d. For reduced curves, normalization has finitely many DVR centres. Each normalized DVR section is one point; regular conductor orders are finite, so full normalization restriction is bijective. Primary powers/units and semilocal gluing give all nonpositive branch functions; G331 positive descent gives envelope min(f,0). This does not identify literal classical/CLD radial extensions. Nilpotents reduce away and dimension-zero reduction has its unique empty envelope.

Six complete immediate BFJ carriers were freshly read, including the complete 3.18 and 3.9--3.10 proofs, at exactly these hypotheses. No normal-surface or positive-characteristic envelope theorem is imported. Full expanded proof: notes/n1.tex. Source ledger: source-application-reading-ledger.md. Rerun: python build_delivery.py; python verify_delivery.py. Execution does not certify the mathematics.

notes.summary: Every full primary-boundary fibre of a finite invariant inclusion is a group orbit, including all nonminimal supports.
notes.detailedSummary: For excellent reduced positive-dimensional local R=S^G with S finite over R, any finite group and any characteristic, orbit-polynomial coefficient ideals give an all-support Gauss identity. Explicit gauge lattice density makes orbit measures lift-independent, proving exact orbit fibres and positive C/D invariant descent. No unnamed field valuation-transitivity theorem, defectlessness or generic-support restriction is assumed.
notes.text:
Let S be excellent reduced local of positive dimension, G a finite group of local automorphisms, R=S^G excellent local, and S finite over R. This theorem needs no characteristic, perfection, faithful action or invertibility of |G|. For every primary a in R, G331 gives the compact surjective restriction rho:V_(aS)(S)->V_a(R), retaining EVERY support. We prove each full fibre is a G orbit.

For a primary/unit S ideal J, choose finite R-module generators b_i and form N_J(T)=product_(sigma in G)(sum_i T_i sigma(b_i)). Its coefficients are invariant, hence in R. Let N_G(J) be their ideal. Linear substitutions in both directions prove independence of module generators. Add generators x of a^N contained in J: pure coefficients x^|G| show N_G(J) contains a boundary power. Proper J gives proper N_G(J) by the positive coefficient-value identity below; units give R.

For any lift w with support P, pass FIRST to the valued quotient fraction field Frac(S/P). Minimum coefficient values multiply: divide by least-valued coefficients and reduce to nonzero residue polynomials, whose product is nonzero. Each factor here has finite minimum because J contains a primary power. Consequently v(N_G(J))=sum_sigma (w composed with sigma)(J), v=rho w, on EVERY support.

These gauges determine finite measures. Their rational difference span is a lattice, since min(wI-wJ,wK-wH)=w(IH+KJ)-w(JH), contains constants from aS, and separates all points by min(w(b),N)=w((b)+(aS)^N). Its uniform closure is all continuous functions: match a target at each pair of points with affine transforms of separating functions; for a fixed first point take a finite maximum to obtain a global lower error bound, then take finitely many minima over first-point neighbourhoods for the upper error bound. This gives arbitrary uniform accuracy on the compact section.

Thus the finite orbit measures sum_sigma delta_(w composed with sigma), all of mass |G|, have integrals determined by v alone. Two lifts have equal measures, first on the gauge lattice, then by uniform density. Their finite supports agree: a continuous function separating a missing point from the other finite support would contradict equality and positive mass. Each lift occurs in its own orbit measure. Therefore rho^{-1}(v)=G.w for EVERY v, simultaneously accounting for support primes and valuation extensions.

Existence of lifts uses G331's full construction: kill the support, choose a prime above it, extend that quotient-field valuation through integral closure and a dominating valuation ring, and use the real algebraic value-group embedding. We import no valuation-extension transitivity theorem and never extend a nonminimal-support semivaluation to S's original fraction field.

The compact bijection Y/G->X is a homeomorphism and the quotient is open, since the saturation of an open U is the union of its translates. G331 POSITIVE descent, not this topology alone, identifies C_R and D_R with the invariant subclasses upstairs. Explicitly -v(N_G(J))/(|G|n) is the orbit average of -w(J)/n and has an actual negative effective ample presentation on its own primary blowup, before limits. Empty boundaries are treated separately. No Monge–Ampere operator or arbitrary nonnormal trace is claimed.

Full proof: notes/n2.tex. Rerun: python exact_checks.py; python build_delivery.py; python verify_delivery.py. The 488 norm-weight instances are finite diagnostics, not proof of full transitivity.

notes.summary: All-dimensional NORMAL finite-group quotient germs have continuous geometric envelopes over algebraically closed characteristic zero.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves invariant-ring finiteness/normality/excellence for smooth affine fixed-point quotients and arbitrary finite continuous actions on regular formal power-series germs. All continuous signed obstacles have a continuous greatest C/D minorant whose pullback is the source envelope. Every canonical degree converges uniformly; signed primary models have error at most |G|(K+M1)/m on every support by orbit coefficient ideals. Positive/mixed-characteristic CE remains conditional on actual source CE; no arbitrary singular regular cover or formal-action algebraization is assumed.
notes.text:
Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic zero. Either B is smooth integral affine over k, G is a finite k-automorphism group fixing a closed point p, S=B_p and R=(B^G)_(p intersect B^G); or S=k[[x_1,...,x_d]] with ANY finite group of continuous local k-automorphisms and R=S^G. In BOTH cases R is an excellent NORMAL local domain, S is finite over R, and EVERY finite continuous signed obstacle on EVERY full normalized primary section of R has a continuous greatest independently geometric C/D minorant. These are complete scoped draft theorems, not general P12.3 closure.

Here are the ring hypotheses. In the affine case, orbit-polynomial coefficients of algebra generators form a finitely generated Noetherian k-subalgebra A0. B is finite over A0; its submodule B^G is finite, hence finitely generated, and B is finite over B^G. An element of Frac(B^G) integral over B^G lies in normal B and is invariant, proving normality. Excellence is finite-type field background. There is only one prime over the marked maximal ideal: a different maximal P would contain b outside p; every translate stays outside the fixed p, but their invariant product belongs to P intersect B^G contained in p, a contradiction. The finite localization is thus B_p, with invariants exactly R.

For formal actions take the orbit-polynomial coefficients of x_i and the image A0 of the formal power-series ring on these coefficients, identified with its kernel quotient. The coefficient ideal in S contains all x_i^|G|. Choose finite monomials spanning its Artinian residue quotient. Repeated residue subtraction expresses every f in S as an A0-linear combination: at step N the remainder is in the Nth coefficient-ideal power contained in m_S^N, and the monomial coefficients converge as formal series. Thus S is finite over complete Noetherian A0. Its invariant submodule R is finite and Noetherian; invariant units have invariant inverses, so R is local. Finite-module completeness and the primary extended base maximal ideal make R complete, hence excellent at the disclosed conventional algebra boundary. Normality follows as above. No algebraization of the action is assumed. Source CE comes from the completed smooth polynomial germ through G331's exact all-support completion and primary contraction.

For a primary gauge a, n2 says EVERY fibre of rho is a G orbit. F=f composed with rho is invariant. Group automorphisms preserve actual models, effectivity and curve degrees, hence permute geometric competitors. The unique source envelope H=P_S F from n1 is therefore invariant. ENTIRE G331 full-fibre POSITIVE descent gives h in C_R with h composed with rho=H. Every target C/D competitor pulls back below H, so surjectivity makes h the greatest one. This proves continuity and the exact envelope pullback formula. These targets are normal, with trivial normalization conductor; the nontrivial finite-cover fibres are the proven group orbits.

Positivity is also explicit: approximate invariant H uniformly by a rational source profile, average its translates, and use n2's orbit coefficient ideal to obtain a downstairs rational primary profile with the same error. Its ACTUAL primary blowup carries a negative effective ample divisor, positive on EVERY contracted integral curve BEFORE limits.

For signed primary models, let J_m=A_m^S(F), which is G stable. Full surjectivity gives EXACT contraction A_m^R(f)=J_m intersect R; extension equality is not claimed. The orbit identity gives N_G(J_m) contained in A_(dm)^R, d=|G|, and h_(dm)^R composed with rho >=h_m^S. If 0<=H-h_m^S<=K/m is n1's precise source model estimate at this gauge, and M1=||v(A_1^R)||, grading for l=dm+s gives h_l^R>=(dm/l)h_(dm)^R-sM1/l>=P_R f-(dK+sM1)/l. The missing fraction of P_R f improves the inequality since P_R f<=0. For l<d use (A_1)^l contained in A_l. Hence 0<=P_R f-h_l^R<=d(K+M1)/l for EVERY l and EVERY support. Nonnegative obstacles use units. Arbitrary continuous obstacles have uniform canonical convergence by n1, without a general rate or FG claim.

Primary cocycles and completion are exact. A decreasing net of continuous obstacles has a greatest D envelope given by its actual decreasing envelope net: it lies below the limit and dominates every competitor termwise, including bottom. This uses no flattening theorem. An explicit singular normal target is k[a,b,c,x_3,...,x_d]_0/(ac-b^2), the quotient changing signs of x_1,x_2. Even-degree monomials generate a=x_1^2,b=x_1x_2,c=x_2^2; reducing powers of b proves the sole relation. Its dimension is d but cotangent dimension d+1 at the origin, so it is singular; the theorem applies in every d>=3 and to its completion.

In positive/mixed characteristic only the conditional transfer with actually established source CE is claimed. We assume no finite regular cover of an arbitrary singular germ. General normal dimension>=3, unrestricted conductor gluing, products, energy and full finite operators remain residual. Full proof: notes/n3.tex and P12.3-quotients-and-wild-conductors.tex. Rerun: python exact_checks.py; python build_delivery.py; python verify_delivery.py.

notes.summary: Same-centre conductor obstruction proved for separable formal covers, including new wild degree-p examples over every characteristic-p field.
notes.detailedSummary: States and proves a conditional full-fibre failure criterion requiring a finite-conductor net and an ALL-downstairs-primary comparison. Verifies it for R=A+yS, u=P(t), ord P=e>=2 and P derivative nonzero, dimension>=3, any field: normalization S has one regular centre, conductor yS, separable degree e, complete algebraic conjugate arcs, and generic monomial comparison. For P=t^p+t^(p+1), L=4, raw p(o)=-4 and every canonical error >=3-p/(p-1)>=1; uniform perturbation stability is proved. No source CE, root-of-unity or perfectness assumption; not a classification of every same-centre fibre or a normal CE failure.
notes.text:
Use ENTIRE qualified G331 and n1. A general conditional same-centre obstruction is as follows. Let an excellent germ have finite normalization S with one marked normal local centre, primary gauge a, regular conductor c and b in S. A full conductor-infinite fibre over o has lifts alpha,beta with alpha(b)=infinity and beta(b)=A finite. Suppose w_i->beta with w_i(c) finite and w_i(b)->A. Suppose a normalized comparison point nu has finite C=nu(c), B=nu(b), and nu(IS)<=K o(I) for EVERY downstairs primary/unit ideal I. For an integer L put D0=1+min(C+B,L)-min(C,L). If eta=D0/K-1-min(A,L)>0, a continuous signed actual-primary obstacle has no greatest geometric C/D minorant; every continuous minorant and EVERY canonical degree has uniform error at least eta.

Proof: cb^n is downstairs by the conductor. Define F=-1-v((cb)+a^L)+v((c)+a^L). On EVERY lift write Y=w(c), z=w(b), allowing infinity; F=-1-[min(Y+z,L)-min(Y,L)]. Both ideals are proper primary. The actual primary T_n=a^n(a^(Ln)+(cb^n)) gives q_n=-1-min(Y/n+z,L)<=F, because the bracket is between zero and min(z,L); infinite cases follow directly from finite truncations. On Bl_(T_n), -E/n is negative effective relatively ample and positive on EVERY contracted integral curve BEFORE limits. At each approaching point sup_n q_n=-1-min(w_i(b),L). The all-primary comparison, negative real sums, uniform comparison and decreasing infima give g(o)<=g(rho nu)/K for EVERY geometric C/D function. A minorant has g(o)<=-D0/K. A greatest minorant would dominate q_n along the approaching net, contradicting USC at o. n1 equates the finite raw suprema. Continuity gives the stated uniform gap for every continuous minorant, hence every canonical degree. Failure persists under ||F'-F||<epsilon when (K+1)epsilon<D0-K(1+min(A,L)), using q_n-epsilon. This is a sufficient conditional theorem, not a fibre-cardinality classification.

All hypotheses are verified in a new broader family. For ANY field k, dimension d>=3, e>=2, Z=(z_1,...,z_(d-3)), take P in k[[T]] of order e with P'(T) nonzero, A=k[[u,y,s,Z]], S=k[[t,y,s,Z]], u=P(t), R=A+yS. Write P=t^e U with U(0) nonzero. Successively reduce a series modulo P to degree<e in t and divide the remainder by P. Since P-adic and t-adic topologies agree, this gives the UNIQUE free basis S=A+ tA+...+t^(e-1)A; uniqueness follows by reduction modulo t^e and repetition. R=A+ytA+...+yt^(e-1)A is a ring because yS is an ideal. It is a finite complete excellent local DOMAIN of dimension d, with m=(u,y,s,Z,yt,...,yt^(e-1)), mS=(P(t),y,s,Z). Modulo the base maximal ideal its extra generators are nilpotent, proving the unique centre. S is regular normal finite over R, and t=(yt)/y, so it is exactly the normalization, with one marked centre.

The conductor is EXACTLY yS. Modulo y the inclusion k[[u,s,Z]] into k[[t,s,Z]] has fraction-field degree e. A nonzero conductor residue a would force every larger element b=(ab)/a into the smaller fraction field, impossible. Conversely yS is conductor. Thus the full conductor quotient is the finite cover u=P(t), with no omitted supports.

There is a nontrivial conjugate arc without root-of-unity or perfection assumptions. The characteristic polynomial Q(T,u) of multiplication by t in the free one-variable basis is monic degree e with Q(T,0)=T^e, and is minimal over k((u)) by the fraction-field degree. The formal change u'=u-P(T) proves Q(T,u)=H(T,u)(u-P(T)), with H(T,0)=-T^e/P(T) a unit. Consequently Q_T(t,P(t))=-H(t,P(t))P'(t) is nonzero, proving separability. Identify one conjugate with s and choose another tau !=s in a finite normal closure L of k((s))/k((u)).

G331 extends the s-adic quotient-field valuation to L. Its integral closure of excellent k[[s]] is finite normal one-dimensional and complete as a finite module. Any semilocal residue idempotent lifts by Newton iteration for x^2-x: 2x-1 is a unit even in characteristic two and errors square. A domain has no nontrivial idempotents, so this integral closure is local, hence a DVR at the ordinary normal-curve foundation. Uniformizer factorization forces the extended valuation to its order, normalized by v(s)=1. The fraction field is complete, since a Cauchy sequence can be scaled into the complete DVR. Conjugates are integral and have positive value by Q(T,0)=T^e. The unit identity then gives P(tau)=P(s); taking values gives v(tau)=1. Hence a=v(tau-s)>=1 is FINITE.

Substitution t=s,y=Z=0 defines alpha; substitution t=tau,y=Z=0 into that complete DVR defines beta. Both have gauge one, kill yS, and agree on EVERY R element: u goes to P(s), s to s, Z to zero, and yS is killed. Their common restriction is o. They differ on t-s, with values infinity and a.

For r>=1 substitute t=tau,Z=0 into O_L[[y]] and use Gauss value min_j(v(c_j)+jr). This minimum is attained and multiplicative: finite initial polynomials multiply nontrivially in the domain gr_v(O_L)[Y]. Formal substitutions converge because t,s have value one. Thus w_r is an actual normalized semivaluation with y-value r and (t-s)-value a. For EVERY fixed series, its y^0 coefficient has finite value N or is zero. If finite, r>N makes all positive-y terms irrelevant; if zero, the value is at least r. Therefore w_r->beta on ALL elements, and restrictions tend to o.

Choose integer L>1+a and use regular coordinates (s,b=t-s,y,Z) with generic monomial weights (1,L,1,1,...). This nu has gauge one and nu(P(t))=e. Every downstairs f with finite o(f)=N has a nonzero pure s^N term when expanded in these coordinates, since setting b=y=Z=0 is precisely o. Positive-weight monomial valuation is at most N; distinct monomials cannot cancel. A generator attaining a primary ideal's finite o-value therefore proves nu(IS)<=o(I) for EVERY downstairs primary/unit ideal. This verifies K=1 without an estimate for every upstairs ideal or a transplanted normal-centre Izumi constant.

Take c=y,b=t-s. The explicit F=-v(m)-v((y(t-s))+m^L)+v((y)+m^L) lies in [-L,-1] on EVERY support, since Y=w(y)>=1 and only finite truncations are subtracted. At nu, F=-L; at o, F=-1. Every geometric minorant has g(o)<=-L, and constant -L is a minorant, so p(o)=-L EXACTLY. Since A_m contains m^(mL), also h_m(o)=-L in EVERY degree. Actual primary competitors T_n=m^n(m^(Ln)+(y(t-s)^n)) satisfy sup_n q_n(rho w_r)=-1-a. The conditional theorem yields no greatest C/D minorant, a non-USC raw envelope, and ||p-h_m||>=L-1-a for EVERY m; the same bound holds for every continuous minorant. Failure is stable under 2epsilon<L-1-a. Source CE is never assumed.

In characteristic p>0 choose P=t^p+t^(p+1). Its order is p but derivative t^p is nonzero, so this is a NEW wild separable degree-p case, outside the old pure-power radicial case. For b=tau-s !=0, P(s+b)-P(s)=b[b^(p-1)(1+s+b)+s^p]=0. The second factor has a unit 1+s+b, giving a=p/(p-1). With L=4, p(o)=h_m(o)=-4 and EVERY error is at least 3-p/(p-1)>=1. These nonnormal formal germs have one regular normalization centre over every characteristic-p field, imperfect fields included.

For another primary gauge d(v)=v(b_primary), canonical ideals are unchanged and the net gap divides by d(o)>0. We assert no exact raw formula elsewhere, no necessary/sufficient classification of all same-centre covers, and no normal CE counterexample. All G331 model/source/audit/radial qualifications remain. Full proof: notes/n4.tex. Finite input/output: exact-check-input.json and reports/exact-checks.json. Rerun: python exact_checks.py; python build_delivery.py; python verify_delivery.py. The finite computations are diagnostics, not the all-support proof.
